introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-001
items.detail: Design a secure monitoring platform for university servers and managed endpoints that collects system events, authentication activity, process information, and security alerts from multiple departments.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: The platform should detect unusual login behavior, repeated failed authentication, suspicious process activity, and unauthorized configuration changes.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003
items.detail: Security administrators should be able to review alerts, investigate affected devices, record investigation notes, change alert status, and isolate compromised endpoints when necessary.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: The system should maintain audit logs of security events and administrator actions and provide a centralized dashboard for monitoring security status across multiple campus locations.

functional.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: collect system events, authentication activity, process information, and security alerts from multiple departments via secure data feeds.
requirements.statement: The system shall collect system events, authentication activity, process information, and security alerts from multiple departments via secure data feeds.

acceptance_criteria.given: A university server with active monitoring enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: System events are generated and transmitted to the platform
acceptance_criteria.then: All event types are received and stored in a normalized format
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of event ingestion from a simulated server

requirements.title: detect unusual login behavior, repeated failed authentication, suspicious process activity, and unauthorized configuration changes using predefined behavioral thresholds.
requirements.statement: The system shall detect unusual login behavior, repeated failed authentication, suspicious process activity, and unauthorized configuration changes using predefined behavioral thresholds.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user attempting multiple failed logins on a managed endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: The platform processes authentication attempts and compares them to baseline behavior
acceptance_criteria.then: An alert is generated for repeated failed authentication events
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of alert generation during simulated attack

requirements.title: Security administrators shall be able to review alerts, investigate affected devices, record investigation notes, change alert status, and isolate compromised endpoints when necessary.
requirements.statement: Security administrators shall be able to review alerts, investigate affected devices, record investigation notes, change alert status, and isolate compromised endpoints when necessary.

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator with access privileges and a test alert from a managed device
acceptance_criteria.when: The administrator requests alert review and performs an investigation
acceptance_criteria.then: The system returns the alert details and allows status update and endpoint isolation
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of alert response and status change

nonfunctional.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: maintain audit logs of security events and administrator actions and provide a centralized dashboard for monitoring security status across multiple campus locations.
requirements.statement: The system shall maintain audit logs of security events and administrator actions and provide a centralized dashboard for monitoring security status across multiple campus locations.

acceptance_criteria.given: A security administrator accesses the system with valid credentials
acceptance_criteria.when: The administrator requests to view audit logs and security status dashboards
acceptance_criteria.then: The system returns audit logs of security events and administrator actions, and displays a centralized dashboard showing current security status across multiple campus locations
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the dashboard display and log retrieval response

open_decisions: Which specific data fields should be included in audit logs?
What is the granularity of security status indicators on the centralized dashboard?
Should real-time updates be provided to the dashboard?
How will endpoint isolation workflows be defined and executed?
What access controls will govern investigation actions during incident response?
What encryption method will be used for data feeds between departments and servers?
What schema will be used to normalize collected events from multiple sources?
What threshold configuration values will trigger alerts for unusual behavior?
What baseline data collection frequency will be maintained for behavioral analysis?

glossary.summary: Source-present terminology; definitions introduce no additional product obligation.

items.title: Device isolation
items.detail: Restriction of a device's network access; the source determines whether and by whom this action is permitted.

items.title: Log
items.detail: A collection of event records. This term does not itself require additional logging fields, events or access permissions.

items.title: Audit record
items.detail: A stored record of an event. Required event scope and retention are determined by the linked source, not this definition.

sdlc.justification: No differentiating input evidence is provided to favor one SDLC model over others. All models receive equal suitability points (40) due to absence of factors such as budget, delivery, failure consequences, feedback, legacy, regulation, schedule, stability, uncertainty, verification. Unknown factors prevent a definitive selection; the decision remains provisional until additional evidence is available.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
